revision.text: [[Category:Https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/]][[ja:%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E9%8A%AD%E6%B9%AF]]

'''Sūpā sentō''' (スーパー銭湯) is one type of public bathhouse in {{ill|Japan|de|Japan|ja|日本|zh|日本}} and a form of {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}}. Under the {{ill|Public Bathhouse Act|de|Public Bathhouse Act (DE)|ja|公衆浴場法|zh|公衆浴場法}} and the public bathhouse ordinances of each {{ill|prefecture|de|Prefecture (DE)|ja|都道府県|zh|都道府県}}, it is classified as an “other public bathhouse” not subject to the regulations of the {{ill|Price Control Ordinance|de|Price Control Ordinance (DE)|ja|物価統制令|zh|物価統制令}}, with facility size and usage fees existing in an intermediate zone between {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} and {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}. It is also included among {{ill|day-trip bathing facilities|de|Day-Trip Bathing Facilities (DE)|ja|日帰り入浴施設|zh|日帰り入浴施設}}. Although there are various theories about where it originated, it is said to have begun appearing in the mid-{{ill|1980s|de|1980er|ja|1980年代|zh|1980年代}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/aichi/ntok0071/list/CK2008102802100033.html|title=スーパー銭湯、サウナ入り放題“発祥” 「お値打ち感」でブームに:なごや特走隊|publisher=中日新聞|website=CHUNICHI Web|date=2007-09-18|archiveurl=https://archive.is/7tcz5|archivedate=2013-04-30|accessdate=2013-04-30|author=白石亘}}[http://yuppon-navi.jp/column/2011/05/3.html 温浴最古論争（3）スーパー銭湯編 日本最初のスーパー銭湯はどこだ?]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（ゆっぽんナビ：温浴おもしろ情報コラム 2011年5月23日）[http://plusplan.exblog.jp/16380175 スーパー銭湯の発祥]（風呂あれこれPartII 2011年8月6日）. While the {{ill|Funabashi Health Center|de|Funabashi Health Center (DE)|ja|船橋ヘルスセンター|zh|船橋ヘルスセンター}} led to the spread of kenkō land facilities nationwide, a new style emerged featuring lower fees, higher turnover, fewer additional facilities, and lower construction costs. These bathing facilities, built around the country with those characteristics, can be called sūpā sentō[http://www.m-brearts.jp/wiki/detail.php?word=%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E9%8A%AD%E6%B9%AF スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（温泉倶楽部：温泉・岩盤浴百科事典）. They differentiate themselves from typical {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} by enhancing optional bath facilities such as outdoor baths (露天風呂), various specialized item baths, and {{ill|sauna|de|Sauna|ja|サウナ風呂|zh|桑拿浴|lt=Sauna|lt_ja=サウナ|lt_de=Sauna|lt_zh=桑拿}}; and by including attached facilities or stores like a {{ill|restaurant|de|Restaurant|ja|外食産業|zh|餐饮业|lt=Dining area}} or a {{ill|barbershop|de|Friseurladen|ja|理髪店|zh|理发店}}, among others. == History == Early examples of facilities that could be called “sūpā sentō,” having more enhanced features, include “Manyō Pokapoka Onsen,” which opened in 1985 in Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture (closed in 2011); “Yume no Kōshū Yokujō Goshiki,” which opened in 1987 in Toyonaka City, Osaka Prefecture; and “New Fujiha Onsen,” which opened in 1976 in Ikuno Ward, Osaka City (closed in 2008). These sentō were classified as “ordinary public bathhouses” under public bathhouse ordinances (where bathing fees are set by each prefecture), so strictly speaking, they differ from the mainstream sūpā sentō in operation today. Meanwhile, “{{ill|Ryūsenji no Yu|de|Ryūsenji no Yu|ja|竜泉寺の湯|zh|竜泉寺の湯}},” which opened in 1989 in Moriyama Ward, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture, is said to be a pioneer of the sūpā sentō classified as “other public bathhouses” under the same ordinances. Its emergence was revolutionary in that the facility could set its own bathing fee and include the sauna fee as part of that bathing fee. From the late {{ill|1990s|de|1990er|ja|1990年代|zh|1990年代}} to the early {{ill|2000s|de|2000er|ja|2000年代|zh|2000年代}}, there was a boom of sūpā sentō openings nationwide, with about 770 facilities opening by 2009[http://summit.ismedia.jp/articles/-/432 なぜスーパー銭湯の乱立が起こったのか]（西川修一、PRESIDENT 2009年9月14日号掲載 / にっぽん経営サミット 2011年1月14日）. From the late 1990s onward, some sūpā sentō began transporting natural hot spring water from nearby onsen by {{ill|truck|de|Lastwagen|ja|貨物自動車|zh|卡车}} to heat and use. This method allows for relatively easy acquisition of natural hot spring water and the freedom to choose from various sources and water qualities. However, since the water is generally used in a circulating system, if large quantities are reused or depending on the equipment, the quality of the water can degrade rapidly. Additionally, since the 2000s, many facilities have started offering add-on services like {{ill|ganbanyoku|de|Ganbanyoku|ja|岩盤浴|zh|岩盤浴}}, and in recent years more places are introducing artificial {{ill|carbonated springs|de|Kohlensäurebad|ja|二酸化炭素泉|zh|二氧化碳温泉|lt=carbon dioxide baths}}. While introducing the latest equipment, many facilities still use a traditional Japanese style of architecture overall{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}. From the late 2010s to the early 2020s, several hot-spring-facility companies based in Aichi Prefecture began expanding into the Greater Tokyo area, ushering in what some call the “Warring States period” of sūpā sentō competition[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (1/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧). On the other hand, as of 2024, facilities built in the early 2000s’ opening rush are hitting or have already passed their general service life of 10 to 20 years, which is typically assumed for hot spring facilities[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854?page=2 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (2/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧). In recent years, an idol group called {{ill|OFR48|de|OFR48 (DE)|ja|OFR48|zh|OFR48}}, formed by female employees working at bathing facilities across the nation to revitalize the bathing industry, has received media coverage{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}. === Children’s mixed-gender bathing age === Regarding the age for children to bathe with the opposite sex, until recently the {{ill|Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|de|Ministerium für Gesundheit, Arbeit und Soziales (Japan)|ja|厚生労働省|zh|厚生労働省}} guidelines for public bathhouse sanitation management set the cut-off at “approximately age 10,” but bathing association groups requested that it be lowered. Based on research conducted under a MHLW grant, in December 2020 the ministry lowered the cut-off to “approximately age 7” and notified each local government厚生労働省「公衆浴場における衛生管理理要領等の改正について〔公衆浴場法〕」(生食発1210第1号)(令和2年12月10日改正)　https://www.mhlw.go.jp/web/t_doc?dataId=00tc5492&dataType=1&pageNo=1. Since sūpā sentō first appeared, “going to the sentō as a family leisure outing” has become common. However, with more families bringing children, concerns have risen over {{ill|mixed-gender bathing|de|Mischbäder (DE)|ja|混浴|zh|混浴}} of children who traditionally would just bathe on the side matching their ({{ill|guardian|de|Vormund|ja|保護者|zh|监护人}}). Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020. == Definition and Features == {{独自研究|section=1|date=2023年5月}} There is no precise definition of sūpā sentō, but in terms of facilities and environment they tend to share the following characteristics[http://zokugo-dict.com/13su/super-sentou.htm スーパー銭湯]（日本語俗語辞典）[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/sentou/sentou_evo1.html 低料金型スーパー銭湯について]/[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/supersentou/gene1.html 第一世代スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（玉岡設計：温浴施設）[http://frat.jp/aloha/past/j09.html 急増するスーパー銭湯]（吉田裕二/ふらっと.jp）[http://mr-planning.com/no1.html スーパー銭湯とは]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（スーパー銭湯を満喫しよう）[http://www.e-tomiya.co.jp/free/30.html 第30回：「スーパー銭湯に行こう!」]（tomiyaフリーポケット）{{cite report|和書|url=https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/servicepolicy/bpo/spa.pdf|title=平成20年度 「我が国におけるスパ・サービスの現状と展望に関する調査研究」報告書|publisher=経済産業省|date=2009-03|accessdate=2020-7-16}}: * They anticipate people arriving by {{ill|car|de|Auto|ja|自動車|zh|汽车}}, so they secure {{ill|parking lots|de|Parkplatz|ja|駐車場|zh|停车场}}. * Relatedly, they often open along main roads in {{ill|suburban|de|Vorstadt|ja|郊外|zh|郊外}} areas. * Besides having an indoor bath, they usually provide item baths such as Jacuzzis, saunas, and outdoor baths. * They include dining space and rest areas. Some places offer a restaurant-level menu. * They have barbershops or {{ill|bodycare|de|Körperpflege|ja|マッサージ|zh|按摩|lt=massage}} shops operating in partnership. * They usually stay open for long hours, from early morning (around 6 to 10am) until late at night (around midnight to 3am). * They rarely close, except for maintenance days. Many are essentially open year-round. Compared with {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}, they generally exhibit the following trends: * Admission fees are set lower. While higher than a normal sentō (due to including a sauna fee, etc.), about 700–800 yen is typical (facilities charging up to around 1,000 yen are generally called sūpā sentō). * Towel rentals are often charged separately; they typically do not provide in-facility clothing as kenkō land might. * Depending on region and facility, some may not furnish complimentary {{ill|shampoo|de|Shampoo|ja|シャンプー|zh|洗发液}} or {{ill|soap|de|Seife|ja|石鹸|zh|肥皂}}, especially in lower-priced establishments. * Few are open 24 hours a day (though some do run overnight hours). * Kenkō land encourages half-day or whole-day stays, but sūpā sentō caters more to shorter visits of around two to three hours. == Major Participating Companies == Because barriers to entry for sūpā sentō are low, various industries have ventured into the market. Some companies, such as {{ill|Gokuraku-yu|de|Gokuraku-yu|ja|極楽湯|zh|極楽湯}}, operate only sūpā sentō facilities. '''Super Sentō''' (スーパー銭湯) is one type of public bathhouse in {{ill|Japan|de|Japan|ja|日本|zh|日本}} and a form of {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}}. Under the {{ill|Public Bathhouse Act|de|Public Bathhouse Act (DE)|ja|公衆浴場法|zh|公衆浴場法}} and the public bathhouse ordinances of each {{ill|prefecture|de|Prefecture (DE)|ja|都道府県|zh|都道府県}}, it is classified as an “other public bathhouse” not subject to the regulations of the {{ill|Price Control Ordinance|de|Price Control Ordinance (DE)|ja|物価統制令|zh|物価統制令}}, with facility size and usage fees existing in an intermediate zone between {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} and {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}. It is also included among {{ill|day-trip bathing facilities|de|Day-Trip Bathing Facilities (DE)|ja|日帰り入浴施設|zh|日帰り入浴施設}}. Although there are various theories about where it originated, it is said to have begun appearing in the mid-{{ill|1980s|de|1980er|ja|1980年代|zh|1980年代}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/aichi/ntok0071/list/CK2008102802100033.html|title=スーパー銭湯、サウナ入り放題“発祥” 「お値打ち感」でブームに:なごや特走隊|publisher=中日新聞|website=CHUNICHI Web|date=2007-09-18|archiveurl=https://archive.is/7tcz5|archivedate=2013-04-30|accessdate=2013-04-30|author=白石亘}}[http://yuppon-navi.jp/column/2011/05/3.html 温浴最古論争（3）スーパー銭湯編 日本最初のスーパー銭湯はどこだ?]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（ゆっぽんナビ：温浴おもしろ情報コラム 2011年5月23日）[http://plusplan.exblog.jp/16380175 スーパー銭湯の発祥]（風呂あれこれPartII 2011年8月6日）. While the {{ill|Funabashi Health Center|de|Funabashi Health Center (DE)|ja|船橋ヘルスセンター|zh|船橋ヘルスセンター}} led to the spread of kenkō land facilities nationwide, a new style emerged featuring lower fees, higher turnover, fewer additional facilities, and lower construction costs. These bathing facilities, built around the country with those characteristics, can be called Super Sentō[http://www.m-brearts.jp/wiki/detail.php?word=%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E9%8A%AD%E6%B9%AF スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（温泉倶楽部：温泉・岩盤浴百科事典）. They differentiate themselves from typical {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} by enhancing optional bath facilities such as outdoor baths (露天風呂), various specialized item baths, and {{ill|sauna|de|Sauna|ja|サウナ風呂|zh|桑拿浴|lt=Sauna|lt_ja=サウナ|lt_de=Sauna|lt_zh=桑拿}}; and by including attached facilities or stores like a {{ill|restaurant|de|Restaurant|ja|外食産業|zh|餐饮业|lt=Dining area}} or a {{ill|barbershop|de|Friseurladen|ja|理髪店|zh|理发店}}, among others. == History == Early examples of facilities that could be called “Super Sentō,” having more enhanced features, include “Manyō Pokapoka Onsen,” which opened in 1985 in Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture (closed in 2011); “Yume no Kōshū Yokujō Goshiki,” which opened in 1987 in Toyonaka City, Osaka Prefecture; and “New Fujiha Onsen,” which opened in 1976 in Ikuno Ward, Osaka City (closed in 2008). These sentō were classified as “ordinary public bathhouses” under public bathhouse ordinances (where bathing fees are set by each prefecture), so strictly speaking, they differ from the mainstream Super Sentō in operation today. Meanwhile, “{{ill|Ryūsenji no Yu|de|Ryūsenji no Yu|ja|竜泉寺の湯|zh|竜泉寺の湯}},” which opened in 1989 in Moriyama Ward, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture, is said to be a pioneer of the Super Sentō classified as “other public bathhouses” under the same ordinances. Its emergence was revolutionary in that the facility could set its own bathing fee and include the sauna fee as part of that bathing fee. From the late {{ill|1990s|de|1990er|ja|1990年代|zh|1990年代}} to the early {{ill|2000s|de|2000er|ja|2000年代|zh|2000年代}}, there was a boom of Super Sentō openings nationwide, with about 770 facilities opening by 2009[http://summit.ismedia.jp/articles/-/432 なぜスーパー銭湯の乱立が起こったのか]（西川修一、PRESIDENT 2009年9月14日号掲載 / にっぽん経営サミット 2011年1月14日）. From the late 1990s onward, some Super Sentō began transporting natural hot spring water from nearby onsen by {{ill|truck|de|Lastwagen|ja|貨物自動車|zh|卡车}} to heat and use. This method allows for relatively easy acquisition of natural hot spring water and the freedom to choose from various sources and water qualities. However, since the water is generally used in a circulating system, if large quantities are reused or depending on the equipment, the quality of the water can degrade rapidly. Additionally, since the 2000s, many facilities have started offering add-on services like {{ill|ganbanyoku|de|Ganbanyoku|ja|岩盤浴|zh|岩盤浴}}, and in recent years more places are introducing artificial {{ill|carbonated springs|de|Kohlensäurebad|ja|二酸化炭素泉|zh|二氧化碳温泉|lt=carbon dioxide baths}}. While introducing the latest equipment, many facilities still use a traditional Japanese style of architecture overall{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}. From the late 2010s to the early 2020s, several hot-spring-facility companies based in Aichi Prefecture began expanding into the Greater Tokyo area, ushering in what some call the “Warring States period” of Super Sentō competition[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (1/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧). On the other hand, as of 2024, facilities built in the early 2000s’ opening rush are hitting or have already passed their general service life of 10 to 20 years, which is typically assumed for hot spring facilities[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854?page=2 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (2/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧). In recent years, an idol group called {{ill|OFR48|de|OFR48 (DE)|ja|OFR48|zh|OFR48}}, formed by female employees working at bathing facilities across the nation to revitalize the bathing industry, has received media coverage{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}. === Children’s mixed-gender bathing age === Regarding the age for children to bathe with the opposite sex, until recently the {{ill|Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|de|Ministerium für Gesundheit, Arbeit und Soziales (Japan)|ja|厚生労働省|zh|厚生労働省}} guidelines for public bathhouse sanitation management set the cut-off at “approximately age 10,” but bathing association groups requested that it be lowered. Based on research conducted under a MHLW grant, in December 2020 the ministry lowered the cut-off to “approximately age 7” and notified each local government厚生労働省「公衆浴場における衛生管理理要領等の改正について〔公衆浴場法〕」(生食発1210第1号)(令和2年12月10日改正)　https://www.mhlw.go.jp/web/t_doc?dataId=00tc5492&dataType=1&pageNo=1. Since Super Sentō first appeared, “going to the sentō as a family leisure outing” has become common. However, with more families bringing children, concerns have risen over {{ill|mixed-gender bathing|de|Mischbäder (DE)|ja|混浴|zh|混浴}} of children who traditionally would just bathe on the side matching their ({{ill|guardian|de|Vormund|ja|保護者|zh|监护人}}). Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020. == Definition and Features == {{独自研究|section=1|date=2023年5月}} There is no precise definition of Super Sentō, but in terms of facilities and environment they tend to share the following characteristics[http://zokugo-dict.com/13su/super-sentou.htm スーパー銭湯]（日本語俗語辞典）[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/sentou/sentou_evo1.html 低料金型スーパー銭湯について]/[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/supersentou/gene1.html 第一世代スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（玉岡設計：温浴施設）[http://frat.jp/aloha/past/j09.html 急増するスーパー銭湯]（吉田裕二/ふらっと.jp）[http://mr-planning.com/no1.html スーパー銭湯とは]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（スーパー銭湯を満喫しよう）[http://www.e-tomiya.co.jp/free/30.html 第30回：「スーパー銭湯に行こう!」]（tomiyaフリーポケット）{{cite report|和書|url=https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/servicepolicy/bpo/spa.pdf|title=平成20年度 「我が国におけるスパ・サービスの現状と展望に関する調査研究」報告書|publisher=経済産業省|date=2009-03|accessdate=2020-7-16}}: * They anticipate people arriving by {{ill|car|de|Auto|ja|自動車|zh|汽车}}, so they secure {{ill|parking lots|de|Parkplatz|ja|駐車場|zh|停车场}}. * Relatedly, they often open along main roads in {{ill|suburban|de|Vorstadt|ja|郊外|zh|郊外}} areas. * Besides having an indoor bath, they usually provide item baths such as Jacuzzis, saunas, and outdoor baths. * They include dining space and rest areas. Some places offer a restaurant-level menu. * They have barbershops or {{ill|bodycare|de|Körperpflege|ja|マッサージ|zh|按摩|lt=massage}} shops operating in partnership. * They usually stay open for long hours, from early morning (around 6 to 10am) until late at night (around midnight to 3am). * They rarely close, except for maintenance days. Many are essentially open year-round. Compared with {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}, they generally exhibit the following trends: * Admission fees are set lower. While higher than a normal sentō (due to including a sauna fee, etc.), about 700–800 yen is typical (facilities charging up to around 1,000 yen are generally called Super Sentō). * Towel rentals are often charged separately; they typically do not provide in-facility clothing as kenkō land might. * Depending on region and facility, some may not furnish complimentary {{ill|shampoo|de|Shampoo|ja|シャンプー|zh|洗发液}} or {{ill|soap|de|Seife|ja|石鹸|zh|肥皂}}, especially in lower-priced establishments. * Few are open 24 hours a day (though some do run overnight hours). * Kenkō land encourages half-day or whole-day stays, but Super Sentō caters more to shorter visits of around two to three hours. == Major Participating Companies == Because barriers to entry for Super Sentō are low, various industries have ventured into the market. Some companies, such as {{ill|Gokuraku-yu|de|Gokuraku-yu|ja|極楽湯|zh|極楽湯}}, operate only Super Sentō facilities. (Facilities marked (F) are {{ill|franchises|de|Franchise|ja|フランチャイズ|zh|特许经营}}.) === Transportation Industry === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:small" |- !Industry!!Company!!Facility Name!!Notes |- |rowspan="9"|{{ill|Railway companies|de|Eisenbahnunternehmen|ja|鉄道事業|zh|铁路公司}}||{{ill|Keisei Electric Railway|de|Keisei Electric Railway|ja|京成電鉄|zh|京成电铁}}||Egao no Yu||Operated by Community Keisei, a group company. |- |{{ill|Keihin Electric Express Railway|de|Keikyu (DE)|ja|京浜急行電鉄|zh|京滨急行电铁}}||{{ill|Miura-yu|de|Miura-yu|ja|みうら湯|zh|みうら湯}}||Operated by {{ill|Keikyu Kaihatsu|de|Keikyu Kaihatsu|ja|京急開発|zh|京急開発}}, a group company. |- |{{ill|Keio Corporation|de|Keio Corporation|ja|京王電鉄|zh|京王电铁}}||{{ill|Keio Takaosan Onsen Gokurakuyu|de|Keio Takaosan Onsen Gokurakuyu|ja|京王高尾山温泉 極楽湯|zh|京王高尾山温泉 極楽湯}} (F)||Operated by {{ill|Keio Setsubi Service|de|Keio Setsubi Service|ja|京王設備サービス|zh|京王設備サービス}}, a group company, as a franchise of {{ill|Gokuraku-yu|de|Gokuraku-yu|ja|極楽湯|zh|極楽湯}}. |- |rowspan="2"|{{ill|Fujikyu|de|Fujikyu (DE)|ja|富士急行|zh|富士急行}}||Fujiyama Onsen||Located next to {{ill|Fuji-Q Highland|de|Fuji-Q Highland|ja|富士急ハイランド|zh|富士急ハイランド}}.

Meanwhile, “{{ill|Ryūsenji no Yu|de|Ryūsenji no Yu|ja|竜泉寺の湯|zh|竜泉寺の湯}},” which opened in 1989 in Moriyama Ward, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture, is said to be a pioneer of the Super Sentō classified as “other public bathhouses” under the same ordinances. Its emergence was revolutionary in that the facility could set its own bathing fee and include the sauna fee as part of that bathing fee. From the late {{ill|1990s|de|1990er|ja|1990年代|zh|1990年代}} to the early {{ill|2000s|de|2000er|ja|2000年代|zh|2000年代}}, there was a boom of Super Sentō openings nationwide, with about 770 facilities opening by 2009[http://summit.ismedia.jp/articles/-/432 なぜスーパー銭湯の乱立が起こったのか]（西川修一、PRESIDENT 2009年9月14日号掲載 / にっぽん経営サミット 2011年1月14日）. From the late 1990s onward, some Super Sentō began transporting natural hot spring water from nearby onsen by {{ill|truck|de|Lastwagen|ja|貨物自動車|zh|卡车}} to heat and use. This method allows for relatively easy acquisition of natural hot spring water and the freedom to choose from various sources and water qualities. However, since the water is generally used in a circulating system, if large quantities are reused or depending on the equipment, the quality of the water can degrade rapidly. Additionally, since the 2000s, many facilities have started offering add-on services like {{ill|ganbanyoku|de|Ganbanyoku|ja|岩盤浴|zh|岩盤浴}}, and in recent years more places are introducing artificial {{ill|carbonated springs|de|Kohlensäurebad|ja|二酸化炭素泉|zh|二氧化碳温泉|lt=carbon dioxide baths}}. While introducing the latest equipment, many facilities still use a traditional Japanese style of architecture overall{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}. From the late 2010s to the early 2020s, several hot-spring-facility companies based in Aichi Prefecture began expanding into the Greater Tokyo area, ushering in what some call the “Warring States period” of Super Sentō competition[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (1/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧). On the other hand, as of 2024, facilities built in the early 2000s’ opening rush are hitting or have already passed their general service life of 10 to 20 years, which is typically assumed for hot spring facilities[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854?page=2 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (2/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧). In recent years, an idol group called {{ill|OFR48|de|OFR48 (DE)|ja|OFR48|zh|OFR48}}, formed by female employees working at bathing facilities across the nation to revitalize the bathing industry, has received media coverage{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}. === Children’s mixed-gender bathing age === Regarding the age for children to bathe with the opposite sex, until recently the {{ill|Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|de|Ministerium für Gesundheit, Arbeit und Soziales (Japan)|ja|厚生労働省|zh|厚生労働省}} guidelines for public bathhouse sanitation management set the cut-off at “approximately age 10,” but bathing association groups requested that it be lowered. Based on research conducted under a MHLW grant, in December 2020 the ministry lowered the cut-off to “approximately age 7” and notified each local government厚生労働省「公衆浴場における衛生管理理要領等の改正について〔公衆浴場法〕」(生食発1210第1号)(令和2年12月10日改正)　https://www.mhlw.go.jp/web/t_doc?dataId=00tc5492&dataType=1&pageNo=1. Since Super Sentō first appeared, “going to the sentō as a family leisure outing” has become common. However, with more families bringing children, concerns have risen over {{ill|mixed-gender bathing|de|Mischbäder (DE)|ja|混浴|1=Mixed bathing|zh|混浴}} of children who traditionally would just bathe on the side matching their ({{ill|guardian|de|Vormund|ja|保護者|zh|监护人}}). Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020. == Definition and Features == {{独自研究|section=1|date=2023年5月}} There is no precise definition of Super Sentō, but in terms of facilities and environment they tend to share the following characteristics[http://zokugo-dict.com/13su/super-sentou.htm スーパー銭湯]（日本語俗語辞典）[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/sentou/sentou_evo1.html 低料金型スーパー銭湯について]/[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/supersentou/gene1.html 第一世代スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（玉岡設計：温浴施設）[http://frat.jp/aloha/past/j09.html 急増するスーパー銭湯]（吉田裕二/ふらっと.jp）[http://mr-planning.com/no1.html スーパー銭湯とは]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（スーパー銭湯を満喫しよう）[http://www.e-tomiya.co.jp/free/30.html 第30回：「スーパー銭湯に行こう!」]（tomiyaフリーポケット）{{cite report|和書|url=https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/servicepolicy/bpo/spa.pdf|title=平成20年度 「我が国におけるスパ・サービスの現状と展望に関する調査研究」報告書|publisher=経済産業省|date=2009-03|accessdate=2020-7-16}}: * They anticipate people arriving by {{ill|car|de|Auto|ja|自動車|zh|汽车}}, so they secure {{ill|parking lots|de|Parkplatz|ja|駐車場|zh|停车场}}. * Relatedly, they often open along main roads in {{ill|suburban|de|Vorstadt|ja|郊外|zh|郊外}} areas. * Besides having an indoor bath, they usually provide item baths such as Jacuzzis, saunas, and outdoor baths. * They include dining space and rest areas. Some places offer a restaurant-level menu. * They have barbershops or {{ill|bodycare|de|Körperpflege|ja|マッサージ|zh|按摩|lt=massage}} shops operating in partnership. * They usually stay open for long hours, from early morning (around 6 to 10am) until late at night (around midnight to 3am). * They rarely close, except for maintenance days. Many are essentially open year-round. Compared with {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}, they generally exhibit the following trends: * Admission fees are set lower. While higher than a normal sentō (due to including a sauna fee, etc.), about 700–800 yen is typical (facilities charging up to around 1,000 yen are generally called Super Sentō). * Towel rentals are often charged separately; they typically do not provide in-facility clothing as kenkō land might. * Depending on region and facility, some may not furnish complimentary {{ill|shampoo|de|Shampoo|ja|シャンプー|zh|洗发液}} or {{ill|soap|de|Seife|ja|石鹸|zh|肥皂}}, especially in lower-priced establishments. * Few are open 24 hours a day (though some do run overnight hours). * Kenkō land encourages half-day or whole-day stays, but Super Sentō caters more to shorter visits of around two to three hours. == Major Participating Companies == Because barriers to entry for Super Sentō are low, various industries have ventured into the market. Some companies, such as {{ill|Gokuraku-yu|de|Gokuraku-yu|ja|極楽湯|zh|極楽湯}}, operate only Super Sentō facilities. Under the {{ill|Public Bathhouse Act|de|Public Bathhouse Act (DE)|ja|公衆浴場法|zh|公衆浴場法}} and the public bathhouse ordinances of each {{ill|prefecture|de|Prefecture (DE)|ja|都道府県|zh|都道府県}}, it is classified as an “other public bathhouse” not subject to the regulations of the {{ill|Price Control Ordinance|de|Price Control Ordinance (DE)|ja|物価統制令|zh|物価統制令}}, with facility size and usage fees existing in an intermediate zone between {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} and {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}. Although there are various theories about where it originated, it is said to have begun appearing in the mid-{{ill|1980s|de|1980er|ja|1980年代|zh|1980年代}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/aichi/ntok0071/list/CK2008102802100033.html|title=スーパー銭湯、サウナ入り放題“発祥” 「お値打ち感」でブームに:なごや特走隊|publisher=中日新聞|website=CHUNICHI Web|date=2007-09-18|archiveurl=https://archive.is/7tcz5|archivedate=2013-04-30|accessdate=2013-04-30|author=白石亘}}[http://yuppon-navi.jp/column/2011/05/3.html 温浴最古論争（3）スーパー銭湯編 日本最初のスーパー銭湯はどこだ?]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（ゆっぽんナビ：温浴おもしろ情報コラム 2011年5月23日）[http://plusplan.exblog.jp/16380175 スーパー銭湯の発祥]（風呂あれこれPartII 2011年8月6日）. Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020. == Definition and Features == {{独自研究|section=1|date=2023年5月}} There is no precise definition of Super Sentō, but in terms of facilities and environment they tend to share the following characteristics[http://zokugo-dict.com/13su/super-sentou.htm スーパー銭湯]（日本語俗語辞典）[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/sentou/sentou_evo1.html 低料金型スーパー銭湯について]/[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/supersentou/gene1.html 第一世代スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（玉岡設計：温浴施設）[http://frat.jp/aloha/past/j09.html 急増するスーパー銭湯]（吉田裕二/ふらっと.jp）[http://mr-planning.com/no1.html スーパー銭湯とは]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（スーパー銭湯を満喫しよう）[http://www.e-tomiya.co.jp/free/30.html 第30回：「スーパー銭湯に行こう!」]（tomiyaフリーポケット）{{cite report|和書|url=https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/servicepolicy/bpo/spa.pdf|title=平成20年度 「我が国におけるスパ・サービスの現状と展望に関する調査研究」報告書|publisher=経済産業省|date=2009-03|accessdate=2020-7-16}}: * They anticipate people arriving by {{ill|car|de|Auto|ja|自動車|zh|汽车}}, so they secure {{ill|parking lots|de|Parkplatz|ja|駐車場|zh|停车场}}. * Relatedly, they often open along main roads in {{ill|suburban|de|Vorstadt|ja|郊外|zh|郊外}} areas. * Besides having an indoor bath, they usually provide item baths such as Jacuzzis, saunas, and outdoor baths. * They include dining space and rest areas. Some places offer a restaurant-level menu. * They have barbershops or {{ill|bodycare|de|Körperpflege|ja|マッサージ|zh|按摩|lt=massage}} shops operating in partnership. * They usually stay open for long hours, from early morning (around 6 to 10am) until late at night (around midnight to 3am). * They rarely close, except for maintenance days. Many are essentially open year-round. Compared with {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}, they generally exhibit the following trends: * Admission fees are set lower. While higher than a normal sentō (due to including a sauna fee, etc.), about 700–800 yen is typical (facilities charging up to around 1,000 yen are generally called Super Sentō). * Towel rentals are often charged separately; they typically do not provide in-facility clothing as kenkō land might. * Depending on region and facility, some may not furnish complimentary {{ill|shampoo|de|Shampoo|ja|シャンプー|zh|洗发液}} or {{ill|soap|de|Seife|ja|石鹸|zh|肥皂}}, especially in lower-priced establishments. * Few are open 24 hours a day (though some do run overnight hours). * Kenkō land encourages half-day or whole-day stays, but Super Sentō caters more to shorter visits of around two to three hours. == Major Participating Companies == Because barriers to entry for Super Sentō are low, various industries have ventured into the market. Some companies, such as {{ill|Gokuraku-yu|de|Gokuraku-yu|ja|極楽湯|zh|極楽湯}}, operate only Super Sentō facilities. [[File:Gokurakuyu Natori.JPG|thumb|A Super Sento run by {{ill|Gokuraku-yu|de|Gokuraku-yu|ja|極楽湯|zh|極楽湯}}]] '''Super Sentō''' (スーパー銭湯) is one type of public bathhouse in {{ill|Japan|de|Japan|ja|日本|zh|日本}} and a form of {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}}.
Under the {{ill|Public Bathhouse Act|de|Public Bathhouse Act (DE)|ja|公衆浴場法|zh|公衆浴場法}} and the public bathhouse ordinances of each {{ill|prefecture|de|Prefecture (DE)|ja|都道府県|zh|都道府県}}, it is classified as an “other public bathhouse” not subject to the regulations of the {{ill|Price Control Ordinance|de|Price Control Ordinance (DE)|ja|物価統制令|zh|物価統制令}}, with facility size and usage fees existing in an intermediate zone between {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} and {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}. It is also included among {{ill|day-trip bathing facilities|de|Day-Trip Bathing Facilities (DE)|ja|日帰り入浴施設|zh|日帰り入浴施設}}.
Although there are various theories about where it originated, it is said to have begun appearing in the mid-{{ill|1980s|de|1980er|ja|1980年代|zh|1980年代}}<ref name="chunichi070918">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/aichi/ntok0071/list/CK2008102802100033.html|title=スーパー銭湯、サウナ入り放題“発祥” 「お値打ち感」でブームに:なごや特走隊|publisher=中日新聞|website=CHUNICHI Web|date=2007-09-18|archiveurl=https://archive.is/7tcz5|archivedate=2013-04-30|accessdate=2013-04-30|author=白石亘}}</ref><ref name="yuppon110523">[http://yuppon-navi.jp/column/2011/05/3.html 温浴最古論争（3）スーパー銭湯編 日本最初のスーパー銭湯はどこだ?]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（ゆっぽんナビ：温浴おもしろ情報コラム 2011年5月23日）</ref><ref name="furoare110806">[http://plusplan.exblog.jp/16380175 スーパー銭湯の発祥]（風呂あれこれPartII 2011年8月6日）</ref>. While the {{ill|Funabashi Health Center|de|Funabashi Health Center (DE)|ja|船橋ヘルスセンター|zh|船橋ヘルスセンター}} led to the spread of kenkō land facilities nationwide, a new style emerged featuring lower fees, higher turnover, fewer additional facilities, and lower construction costs. These bathing facilities, built around the country with those characteristics, can be called Super Sentō<ref name="onsenkurabu-jiten">[http://www.m-brearts.jp/wiki/detail.php?word=%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E9%8A%AD%E6%B9%AF スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（温泉倶楽部：温泉・岩盤浴百科事典）</ref>.
They differentiate themselves from typical {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} by enhancing optional bath facilities such as outdoor baths (露天風呂), various specialized item baths, and {{ill|sauna|de|Sauna|ja|サウナ風呂|zh|桑拿浴|lt=Sauna|lt_ja=サウナ|lt_de=Sauna|lt_zh=桑拿}}; and by including attached facilities or stores like a {{ill|restaurant|de|Restaurant|ja|外食産業|zh|餐饮业|lt=Dining area}} or a {{ill|barbershop|de|Friseurladen|ja|理髪店|zh|理发店}}, among others.
== History == Early examples of facilities that could be called “Super Sentō,” having more enhanced features, include “Manyō Pokapoka Onsen,” which opened in 1985 in Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture (closed in 2011); “Yume no Kōshū Yokujō Goshiki,” which opened in 1987 in Toyonaka City, Osaka Prefecture; and “New Fujiha Onsen,” which opened in 1976 in Ikuno Ward, Osaka City (closed in 2008). These sentō were classified as “ordinary public bathhouses” under public bathhouse ordinances (where bathing fees are set by each prefecture), so strictly speaking, they differ from the mainstream Super Sentō in operation today. Meanwhile, “{{ill|Ryūsenji no Yu|de|Ryūsenji no Yu|ja|竜泉寺の湯|zh|竜泉寺の湯}},” which opened in 1989 in Moriyama Ward, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture, is said to be a pioneer of the Super Sentō classified as “other public bathhouses” under the same ordinances. Its emergence was revolutionary in that the facility could set its own bathing fee and include the sauna fee as part of that bathing fee<ref name="chunichi070918"/><ref name="yuppon110523"/><ref name="furoare110806"/>. From the late {{ill|1990s|de|1990er|ja|1990年代|zh|1990年代}} to the early {{ill|2000s|de|2000er|ja|2000年代|zh|2000年代}}, there was a boom of Super Sentō openings nationwide, with about 770 facilities opening by 2009<ref>[http://summit.ismedia.jp/articles/-/432 なぜスーパー銭湯の乱立が起こったのか]（西川修一、PRESIDENT 2009年9月14日号掲載 / にっぽん経営サミット 2011年1月14日）</ref>.
From the late 1990s onward, some Super Sentō began transporting natural hot spring water from nearby onsen by {{ill|truck|de|Lastwagen|ja|貨物自動車|zh|卡车}} to heat and use. This method allows for relatively easy acquisition of natural hot spring water and the freedom to choose from various sources and water qualities. However, since the water is generally used in a circulating system, if large quantities are reused or depending on the equipment, the quality of the water can degrade rapidly. Additionally, since the 2000s, many facilities have started offering add-on services like {{ill|ganbanyoku|de|Ganbanyoku|ja|岩盤浴|zh|岩盤浴}}, and in recent years more places are introducing artificial {{ill|carbonated springs|de|Kohlensäurebad|ja|二酸化炭素泉|zh|二氧化碳温泉|lt=carbon dioxide baths}}. While introducing the latest equipment, many facilities still use a traditional Japanese style of architecture overall{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}.
From the late 2010s to the early 2020s, several hot-spring-facility companies based in Aichi Prefecture began expanding into the Greater Tokyo area, ushering in what some call the “Warring States period” of Super Sentō competition<ref>[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (1/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧)</ref>. On the other hand, as of 2024, facilities built in the early 2000s’ opening rush are hitting or have already passed their general service life of 10 to 20 years, which is typically assumed for hot spring facilities<ref>[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854?page=2 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (2/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧)</ref>.
In recent years, an idol group called {{ill|OFR48|de|OFR48 (DE)|ja|OFR48|zh|OFR48}}, formed by female employees working at bathing facilities across the nation to revitalize the bathing industry, has received media coverage{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}.
=== Children’s mixed-gender bathing age === Regarding the age for children to bathe with the opposite sex, until recently the {{ill|Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|de|Ministerium für Gesundheit, Arbeit und Soziales (Japan)|ja|厚生労働省|zh|厚生労働省}} guidelines for public bathhouse sanitation management set the cut-off at “approximately age 10,” but bathing association groups requested that it be lowered. Based on research conducted under a MHLW grant, in December 2020 the ministry lowered the cut-off to “approximately age 7” and notified each local government<ref>厚生労働省「公衆浴場における衛生管理理要領等の改正について〔公衆浴場法〕」(生食発1210第1号)(令和2年12月10日改正) https://www.mhlw.go.jp/web/t_doc?dataId=00tc5492&dataType=1&pageNo=1</ref>.
Since Super Sentō first appeared, “going to the sentō as a family leisure outing” has become common. However, with more families bringing children, concerns have risen over {{ill|mixed-gender bathing|de|Mischbäder (DE)|ja|混浴|1=Mixed bathing|zh|混浴}} of children who traditionally would just bathe on the side matching their ({{ill|guardian|de|Vormund|ja|保護者|zh|监护人}}). Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020.

Some places offer a restaurant-level menu. * They have barbershops or {{ill|bodycare|de|Körperpflege|ja|マッサージ|zh|按摩|lt=massage}} shops operating in partnership. * They usually stay open for long hours, from early morning (around 6 to 10am) until late at night (around midnight to 3am). * They rarely close, except for maintenance days. Many are essentially open year-round.
Compared with {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}, they generally exhibit the following trends: * Admission fees are set lower. While higher than a normal sentō (due to including a sauna fee, etc.), about 700–800 yen is typical (facilities charging up to around 1,000 yen are generally called Super Sentō). * Towel rentals are often charged separately; they typically do not provide in-facility clothing as kenkō land might. * Depending on region and facility, some may not furnish complimentary {{ill|shampoo|de|Shampoo|ja|シャンプー|zh|洗发液}} or {{ill|soap|de|Seife|ja|石鹸|zh|肥皂}}, especially in lower-priced establishments. * Few are open 24 hours a day (though some do run overnight hours). * Kenkō land encourages half-day or whole-day stays, but Super Sentō caters more to shorter visits of around two to three hours.

[[category:completion tier 1]][[ja:スーパー銭湯]][[de:Super Sento]] [[Category:Https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/]][[ja:%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E9%8A%AD%E6%B9%AF]] {{Onsen}}

[[File:Gokurakuyu Natori.JPG|thumb|A Super Sento run by {{ill|Gokuraku-yu|de|Gokuraku-yu|ja|極楽湯|zh|極楽湯}}]] '''Super Sentō''' (スーパー銭湯) is one type of public bathhouse in {{ill|Japan|de|Japan|ja|日本|zh|日本}} and a form of {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}}.
Under the {{ill|Public Bathhouse Act|de|Public Bathhouse Act (DE)|ja|公衆浴場法|zh|公衆浴場法}} and the public bathhouse ordinances of each {{ill|prefecture|de|Prefecture (DE)|ja|都道府県|zh|都道府県}}, it is classified as an “other public bathhouse” not subject to the regulations of the {{ill|Price Control Ordinance|de|Price Control Ordinance (DE)|ja|物価統制令|zh|物価統制令}}, with facility size and usage fees existing in an intermediate zone between {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} and {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}. It is also included among {{ill|day-trip bathing facilities|de|Day-Trip Bathing Facilities (DE)|ja|日帰り入浴施設|zh|日帰り入浴施設}}.
Although there are various theories about where it originated, it is said to have begun appearing in the mid-{{ill|1980s|de|1980er|ja|1980年代|zh|1980年代}}<ref name="chunichi070918">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/aichi/ntok0071/list/CK2008102802100033.html|title=スーパー銭湯、サウナ入り放題“発祥” 「お値打ち感」でブームに:なごや特走隊|publisher=中日新聞|website=CHUNICHI Web|date=2007-09-18|archiveurl=https://archive.is/7tcz5|archivedate=2013-04-30|accessdate=2013-04-30|author=白石亘}}</ref><ref name="yuppon110523">[http://yuppon-navi.jp/column/2011/05/3.html 温浴最古論争（3）スーパー銭湯編 日本最初のスーパー銭湯はどこだ?]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（ゆっぽんナビ：温浴おもしろ情報コラム 2011年5月23日）</ref><ref name="furoare110806">[http://plusplan.exblog.jp/16380175 スーパー銭湯の発祥]（風呂あれこれPartII 2011年8月6日）</ref>. While the {{ill|Funabashi Health Center|de|Funabashi Health Center (DE)|ja|船橋ヘルスセンター|zh|船橋ヘルスセンター}} led to the spread of kenkō land facilities nationwide, a new style emerged featuring lower fees, higher turnover, fewer additional facilities, and lower construction costs. These bathing facilities, built around the country with those characteristics, can be called Super Sentō<ref name="onsenkurabu-jiten">[http://www.m-brearts.jp/wiki/detail.php?word=%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E9%8A%AD%E6%B9%AF スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（温泉倶楽部：温泉・岩盤浴百科事典）</ref>.
They differentiate themselves from typical {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} by enhancing optional bath facilities such as outdoor baths (露天風呂), various specialized item baths, and {{ill|sauna|de|Sauna|ja|サウナ風呂|zh|桑拿浴|lt=Sauna|lt_ja=サウナ|lt_de=Sauna|lt_zh=桑拿}}; and by including attached facilities or stores like a {{ill|restaurant|de|Restaurant|ja|外食産業|zh|餐饮业|lt=Dining area}} or a {{ill|barbershop|de|Friseurladen|ja|理髪店|zh|理发店}}, among others.
== History == Early examples of facilities that could be called “Super Sentō,” having more enhanced features, include “Manyō Pokapoka Onsen,” which opened in 1985 in Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture (closed in 2011); “Yume no Kōshū Yokujō Goshiki,” which opened in 1987 in Toyonaka City, Osaka Prefecture; and “New Fujiha Onsen,” which opened in 1976 in Ikuno Ward, Osaka City (closed in 2008). These sentō were classified as “ordinary public bathhouses” under public bathhouse ordinances (where bathing fees are set by each prefecture), so strictly speaking, they differ from the mainstream Super Sentō in operation today. Meanwhile, “{{ill|Ryūsenji no Yu|de|Ryūsenji no Yu|ja|竜泉寺の湯|zh|竜泉寺の湯}},” which opened in 1989 in Moriyama Ward, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture, is said to be a pioneer of the Super Sentō classified as “other public bathhouses” under the same ordinances. Its emergence was revolutionary in that the facility could set its own bathing fee and include the sauna fee as part of that bathing fee<ref name="chunichi070918"/><ref name="yuppon110523"/><ref name="furoare110806"/>. From the late {{ill|1990s|de|1990er|ja|1990年代|zh|1990年代}} to the early {{ill|2000s|de|2000er|ja|2000年代|zh|2000年代}}, there was a boom of Super Sentō openings nationwide, with about 770 facilities opening by 2009<ref>[http://summit.ismedia.jp/articles/-/432 なぜスーパー銭湯の乱立が起こったのか]（西川修一、PRESIDENT 2009年9月14日号掲載 / にっぽん経営サミット 2011年1月14日）</ref>.
From the late 1990s onward, some Super Sentō began transporting natural hot spring water from nearby onsen by {{ill|truck|de|Lastwagen|ja|貨物自動車|zh|卡车}} to heat and use. This method allows for relatively easy acquisition of natural hot spring water and the freedom to choose from various sources and water qualities. However, since the water is generally used in a circulating system, if large quantities are reused or depending on the equipment, the quality of the water can degrade rapidly. Additionally, since the 2000s, many facilities have started offering add-on services like {{ill|ganbanyoku|de|Ganbanyoku|ja|岩盤浴|zh|岩盤浴}}, and in recent years more places are introducing artificial {{ill|carbonated springs|de|Kohlensäurebad|ja|二酸化炭素泉|zh|二氧化碳温泉|lt=carbon dioxide baths}}. While introducing the latest equipment, many facilities still use a traditional Japanese style of architecture overall{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}.
From the late 2010s to the early 2020s, several hot-spring-facility companies based in Aichi Prefecture began expanding into the Greater Tokyo area, ushering in what some call the “Warring States period” of Super Sentō competition<ref>[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (1/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧)</ref>. On the other hand, as of 2024, facilities built in the early 2000s’ opening rush are hitting or have already passed their general service life of 10 to 20 years, which is typically assumed for hot spring facilities<ref>[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854?page=2 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (2/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧)</ref>.
In recent years, an idol group called {{ill|OFR48|de|OFR48 (DE)|ja|OFR48|zh|OFR48}}, formed by female employees working at bathing facilities across the nation to revitalize the bathing industry, has received media coverage{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}.
=== Children’s mixed-gender bathing age === Regarding the age for children to bathe with the opposite sex, until recently the {{ill|Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|de|Ministerium für Gesundheit, Arbeit und Soziales (Japan)|ja|厚生労働省|zh|厚生労働省}} guidelines for public bathhouse sanitation management set the cut-off at “approximately age 10,” but bathing association groups requested that it be lowered. Based on research conducted under a MHLW grant, in December 2020 the ministry lowered the cut-off to “approximately age 7” and notified each local government<ref>厚生労働省「公衆浴場における衛生管理理要領等の改正について〔公衆浴場法〕」(生食発1210第1号)(令和2年12月10日改正) https://www.mhlw.go.jp/web/t_doc?dataId=00tc5492&dataType=1&pageNo=1</ref>.
Since Super Sentō first appeared, “going to the sentō as a family leisure outing” has become common. However, with more families bringing children, concerns have risen over {{ill|mixed-gender bathing|de|Mischbäder (DE)|ja|混浴|1=Mixed bathing|zh|混浴}} of children who traditionally would just bathe on the side matching their ({{ill|guardian|de|Vormund|ja|保護者|zh|监护人}}). Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020.
== Definition and Features == {{独自研究|section=1|date=2023年5月}} There is no precise definition of Super Sentō, but in terms of facilities and environment they tend to share the following characteristics<ref name="onsenkurabu-jiten"/><ref>[http://zokugo-dict.com/13su/super-sentou.htm スーパー銭湯]（日本語俗語辞典）</ref><ref>[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/sentou/sentou_evo1.html 低料金型スーパー銭湯について]/[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/supersentou/gene1.html 第一世代スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（玉岡設計：温浴施設）</ref><ref>[http://frat.jp/aloha/past/j09.html 急増するスーパー銭湯]（吉田裕二/ふらっと.jp）</ref><ref>[http://mr-planning.com/no1.html スーパー銭湯とは]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（スーパー銭湯を満喫しよう）</ref><ref>[http://www.e-tomiya.co.jp/free/30.html 第30回：「スーパー銭湯に行こう!」]（tomiyaフリーポケット）</ref><ref>{{cite report|和書|url=https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/servicepolicy/bpo/spa.pdf|title=平成20年度 「我が国におけるスパ・サービスの現状と展望に関する調査研究」報告書|publisher=経済産業省|date=2009-03|accessdate=2020-7-16}}</ref>: * They anticipate people arriving by {{ill|car|de|Auto|ja|自動車|zh|汽车}}, so they secure {{ill|parking lots|de|Parkplatz|ja|駐車場|zh|停车场}}. * Relatedly, they often open along main roads in {{ill|suburban|de|Vorstadt|ja|郊外|zh|郊外}} areas. * Besides having an indoor bath, they usually provide item baths such as Jacuzzis, saunas, and outdoor baths. * They include dining space and rest areas. Some places offer a restaurant-level menu. * They have barbershops or {{ill|bodycare|de|Körperpflege|ja|マッサージ|zh|按摩|lt=massage}} shops operating in partnership. * They usually stay open for long hours, from early morning (around 6 to 10am) until late at night (around midnight to 3am). * They rarely close, except for maintenance days. Many are essentially open year-round.
Compared with {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|zh|健康ランド}}, they generally exhibit the following trends: * Admission fees are set lower. While higher than a normal sentō (due to including a sauna fee, etc.), about 700–800 yen is typical (facilities charging up to around 1,000 yen are generally called Super Sentō). * Towel rentals are often charged separately; they typically do not provide in-facility clothing as kenkō land might. * Depending on region and facility, some may not furnish complimentary {{ill|shampoo|de|Shampoo|ja|シャンプー|zh|洗发液}} or {{ill|soap|de|Seife|ja|石鹸|zh|肥皂}}, especially in lower-priced establishments. * Few are open 24 hours a day (though some do run overnight hours). * Kenkō land encourages half-day or whole-day stays, but Super Sentō caters more to shorter visits of around two to three hours.

On the other hand, as of 2024, facilities built in the early 2000s’ opening rush are hitting or have already passed their general service life of 10 to 20 years, which is typically assumed for hot spring facilities<ref>[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854?page=2 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (2/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧)</ref>.
In recent years, an idol group called {{ill|OFR48|de|OFR48 (DE)|ja|OFR48|zh|OFR48}}, formed by female employees working at bathing facilities across the nation to revitalize the bathing industry, has received media coverage{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}.
=== Children’s mixed-gender bathing age === Regarding the age for children to bathe with the opposite sex, until recently the {{ill|Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|de|Ministerium für Gesundheit, Arbeit und Soziales (Japan)|ja|厚生労働省|zh|厚生労働省}} guidelines for public bathhouse sanitation management set the cut-off at “approximately age 10,” but bathing association groups requested that it be lowered. Based on research conducted under a MHLW grant, in December 2020 the ministry lowered the cut-off to “approximately age 7” and notified each local government<ref>厚生労働省「公衆浴場における衛生管理理要領等の改正について〔公衆浴場法〕」(生食発1210第1号)(令和2年12月10日改正) https://www.mhlw.go.jp/web/t_doc?dataId=00tc5492&dataType=1&pageNo=1</ref>.
Since Super Sentō first appeared, “going to the sentō as a family leisure outing” has become common. However, with more families bringing children, concerns have risen over {{ill|mixed-gender bathing|de|Mischbäder (DE)|ja|混浴|1=Mixed bathing|zh|混浴}} of children who traditionally would just bathe on the side matching their ({{ill|guardian|de|Vormund|ja|保護者|zh|监护人}}). Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020.
== Definition and Features == {{独自研究|section=1|date=2023年5月}} There is no precise definition of Super Sentō, but in terms of facilities and environment they tend to share the following characteristics<ref name="onsenkurabu-jiten"/><ref>[http://zokugo-dict.com/13su/super-sentou.htm スーパー銭湯]（日本語俗語辞典）</ref><ref>[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/sentou/sentou_evo1.html 低料金型スーパー銭湯について]/[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/supersentou/gene1.html 第一世代スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（玉岡設計：温浴施設）</ref><ref>[http://frat.jp/aloha/past/j09.html 急増するスーパー銭湯]（吉田裕二/ふらっと.jp）</ref><ref>[http://mr-planning.com/no1.html スーパー銭湯とは]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（スーパー銭湯を満喫しよう）</ref><ref>[http://www.e-tomiya.co.jp/free/30.html 第30回：「スーパー銭湯に行こう!」]（tomiyaフリーポケット）</ref><ref>{{cite report|和書|url=https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/servicepolicy/bpo/spa.pdf|title=平成20年度 「我が国におけるスパ・サービスの現状と展望に関する調査研究」報告書|publisher=経済産業省|date=2009-03|accessdate=2020-7-16}}</ref>: * They anticipate people arriving by {{ill|car|de|Auto|ja|自動車|zh|汽车}}, so they secure {{ill|parking lots|de|Parkplatz|ja|駐車場|zh|停车场}}. * Relatedly, they often open along main roads in {{ill|suburban|de|Vorstadt|ja|郊外|zh|郊外}} areas. * Besides having an indoor bath, they usually provide item baths such as Jacuzzis, saunas, and outdoor baths. * They include dining space and rest areas. Some places offer a restaurant-level menu. * They have barbershops or {{ill|bodycare|de|Körperpflege|ja|マッサージ|zh|按摩|lt=massage}} shops operating in partnership. * They usually stay open for long hours, from early morning (around 6 to 10am) until late at night (around midnight to 3am). * They rarely close, except for maintenance days. Many are essentially open year-round.
Compared with {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|1=Health land|zh|健康ランド}}, they generally exhibit the following trends: * Admission fees are set lower. While higher than a normal sentō (due to including a sauna fee, etc.), about 700–800 yen is typical (facilities charging up to around 1,000 yen are generally called Super Sentō). * Towel rentals are often charged separately; they typically do not provide in-facility clothing as kenkō land might. * Depending on region and facility, some may not furnish complimentary {{ill|shampoo|de|Shampoo|ja|シャンプー|zh|洗发液}} or {{ill|soap|de|Seife|ja|石鹸|zh|肥皂}}, especially in lower-priced establishments. * Few are open 24 hours a day (though some do run overnight hours). * Kenkō land encourages half-day or whole-day stays, but Super Sentō caters more to shorter visits of around two to three hours.

[[File:Gokurakuyu Natori.JPG|thumb|A Super Sento run by {{ill|Gokuraku-yu|de|Gokuraku-yu|ja|極楽湯|zh|極楽湯}}]] '''Super Sentō''' (スーパー銭湯) is one type of public bathhouse in {{ill|Japan|de|Japan|ja|日本|zh|日本}} and a form of {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}}.
Under the {{ill|Public Bathhouse Act|de|Public Bathhouse Act (DE)|ja|公衆浴場法|zh|公衆浴場法}} and the public bathhouse ordinances of each {{ill|prefecture|de|Prefecture (DE)|ja|都道府県|zh|都道府県}}, it is classified as an “other public bathhouse” not subject to the regulations of the {{ill|Price Control Ordinance|de|Price Control Ordinance (DE)|ja|物価統制令|zh|物価統制令}}, with facility size and usage fees existing in an intermediate zone between {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} and {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|1=Health land|zh|健康ランド}}. It is also included among {{ill|day-trip bathing facilities|de|Day-Trip Bathing Facilities (DE)|ja|日帰り入浴施設|zh|日帰り入浴施設}}.
Although there are various theories about where it originated, it is said to have begun appearing in the mid-{{ill|1980s|de|1980er|ja|1980年代|zh|1980年代}}<ref name="chunichi070918">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/aichi/ntok0071/list/CK2008102802100033.html|title=スーパー銭湯、サウナ入り放題“発祥” 「お値打ち感」でブームに:なごや特走隊|publisher=中日新聞|website=CHUNICHI Web|date=2007-09-18|archiveurl=https://archive.is/7tcz5|archivedate=2013-04-30|accessdate=2013-04-30|author=白石亘}}</ref><ref name="yuppon110523">[http://yuppon-navi.jp/column/2011/05/3.html 温浴最古論争（3）スーパー銭湯編 日本最初のスーパー銭湯はどこだ?]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（ゆっぽんナビ：温浴おもしろ情報コラム 2011年5月23日）</ref><ref name="furoare110806">[http://plusplan.exblog.jp/16380175 スーパー銭湯の発祥]（風呂あれこれPartII 2011年8月6日）</ref>. While the {{ill|Funabashi Health Center|de|Funabashi Health Center (DE)|ja|船橋ヘルスセンター|zh|船橋ヘルスセンター}} led to the spread of kenkō land facilities nationwide, a new style emerged featuring lower fees, higher turnover, fewer additional facilities, and lower construction costs. These bathing facilities, built around the country with those characteristics, can be called Super Sentō<ref name="onsenkurabu-jiten">[http://www.m-brearts.jp/wiki/detail.php?word=%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E9%8A%AD%E6%B9%AF スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（温泉倶楽部：温泉・岩盤浴百科事典）</ref>.
They differentiate themselves from typical {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} by enhancing optional bath facilities such as outdoor baths (露天風呂), various specialized item baths, and {{ill|sauna|de|Sauna|ja|サウナ風呂|zh|桑拿浴|lt=Sauna|lt_ja=サウナ|lt_de=Sauna|lt_zh=桑拿}}; and by including attached facilities or stores like a {{ill|restaurant|de|Restaurant|ja|外食産業|zh|餐饮业|lt=Dining area}} or a {{ill|barbershop|de|Friseurladen|ja|理髪店|zh|理发店}}, among others.
== History == Early examples of facilities that could be called “Super Sentō,” having more enhanced features, include “Manyō Pokapoka Onsen,” which opened in 1985 in Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture (closed in 2011); “Yume no Kōshū Yokujō Goshiki,” which opened in 1987 in Toyonaka City, Osaka Prefecture; and “New Fujiha Onsen,” which opened in 1976 in Ikuno Ward, Osaka City (closed in 2008). These sentō were classified as “ordinary public bathhouses” under public bathhouse ordinances (where bathing fees are set by each prefecture), so strictly speaking, they differ from the mainstream Super Sentō in operation today. Meanwhile, “{{ill|Ryūsenji no Yu|de|Ryūsenji no Yu|ja|竜泉寺の湯|zh|竜泉寺の湯}},” which opened in 1989 in Moriyama Ward, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture, is said to be a pioneer of the Super Sentō classified as “other public bathhouses” under the same ordinances. Its emergence was revolutionary in that the facility could set its own bathing fee and include the sauna fee as part of that bathing fee<ref name="chunichi070918"/><ref name="yuppon110523"/><ref name="furoare110806"/>. From the late {{ill|1990s|de|1990er|ja|1990年代|zh|1990年代}} to the early {{ill|2000s|de|2000er|ja|2000年代|zh|2000年代}}, there was a boom of Super Sentō openings nationwide, with about 770 facilities opening by 2009<ref>[http://summit.ismedia.jp/articles/-/432 なぜスーパー銭湯の乱立が起こったのか]（西川修一、PRESIDENT 2009年9月14日号掲載 / にっぽん経営サミット 2011年1月14日）</ref>.
From the late 1990s onward, some Super Sentō began transporting natural hot spring water from nearby onsen by {{ill|truck|de|Lastwagen|ja|貨物自動車|zh|卡车}} to heat and use. This method allows for relatively easy acquisition of natural hot spring water and the freedom to choose from various sources and water qualities. However, since the water is generally used in a circulating system, if large quantities are reused or depending on the equipment, the quality of the water can degrade rapidly. Additionally, since the 2000s, many facilities have started offering add-on services like {{ill|ganbanyoku|de|Ganbanyoku|ja|岩盤浴|zh|岩盤浴}}, and in recent years more places are introducing artificial {{ill|carbonated springs|de|Kohlensäurebad|ja|二酸化炭素泉|1=Carbon Dioxide Springs|zh|二氧化碳温泉|lt=carbon dioxide baths}}. While introducing the latest equipment, many facilities still use a traditional Japanese style of architecture overall{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}.
From the late 2010s to the early 2020s, several hot-spring-facility companies based in Aichi Prefecture began expanding into the Greater Tokyo area, ushering in what some call the “Warring States period” of Super Sentō competition<ref>[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (1/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧)</ref>. In recent years, an idol group called {{ill|OFR48|de|OFR48 (DE)|ja|OFR48|zh|OFR48}}, formed by female employees working at bathing facilities across the nation to revitalize the bathing industry, has received media coverage{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}.
=== Children’s mixed-gender bathing age === Regarding the age for children to bathe with the opposite sex, until recently the {{ill|Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|de|Ministerium für Gesundheit, Arbeit und Soziales (Japan)|ja|厚生労働省|zh|厚生労働省}} guidelines for public bathhouse sanitation management set the cut-off at “approximately age 10,” but bathing association groups requested that it be lowered. Based on research conducted under a MHLW grant, in December 2020 the ministry lowered the cut-off to “approximately age 7” and notified each local government<ref>厚生労働省「公衆浴場における衛生管理理要領等の改正について〔公衆浴場法〕」(生食発1210第1号)(令和2年12月10日改正) https://www.mhlw.go.jp/web/t_doc?dataId=00tc5492&dataType=1&pageNo=1</ref>.
Since Super Sentō first appeared, “going to the sentō as a family leisure outing” has become common. However, with more families bringing children, concerns have risen over {{ill|mixed-gender bathing|de|Mischbäder (DE)|ja|混浴|1=Mixed bathing|zh|混浴}} of children who traditionally would just bathe on the side matching their ({{ill|guardian|de|Vormund|ja|保護者|zh|监护人}}). Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020.
== Definition and Features == {{独自研究|section=1|date=2023年5月}} There is no precise definition of Super Sentō, but in terms of facilities and environment they tend to share the following characteristics<ref name="onsenkurabu-jiten"/><ref>[http://zokugo-dict.com/13su/super-sentou.htm スーパー銭湯]（日本語俗語辞典）</ref><ref>[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/sentou/sentou_evo1.html 低料金型スーパー銭湯について]/[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/supersentou/gene1.html 第一世代スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（玉岡設計：温浴施設）</ref><ref>[http://frat.jp/aloha/past/j09.html 急増するスーパー銭湯]（吉田裕二/ふらっと.jp）</ref><ref>[http://mr-planning.com/no1.html スーパー銭湯とは]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（スーパー銭湯を満喫しよう）</ref><ref>[http://www.e-tomiya.co.jp/free/30.html 第30回：「スーパー銭湯に行こう!」]（tomiyaフリーポケット）</ref><ref>{{cite report|和書|url=https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/servicepolicy/bpo/spa.pdf|title=平成20年度 「我が国におけるスパ・サービスの現状と展望に関する調査研究」報告書|publisher=経済産業省|date=2009-03|accessdate=2020-7-16}}</ref>: * They anticipate people arriving by {{ill|car|de|Auto|ja|自動車|zh|汽车}}, so they secure {{ill|parking lots|de|Parkplatz|ja|駐車場|zh|停车场}}. * Relatedly, they often open along main roads in {{ill|suburban|de|Vorstadt|ja|郊外|zh|郊外}} areas. * Besides having an indoor bath, they usually provide item baths such as Jacuzzis, saunas, and outdoor baths. * They include dining space and rest areas. Under the {{ill|Public Bathhouse Act|de|Public Bathhouse Act (DE)|ja|公衆浴場法|zh|公衆浴場法}} and the public bathhouse ordinances of each {{ill|prefecture|de|Prefecture (DE)|ja|都道府県|zh|都道府県}}, it is classified as an “other public bathhouse” not subject to the regulations of the {{ill|Price Control Ordinance|de|Price Control Ordinance (DE)|ja|物価統制令|zh|物価統制令}}, with facility size and usage fees existing in an intermediate zone between {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} and {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|1=Health land|zh|健康ランド}}. It is also included among {{ill|day-trip bathing facilities|de|Day-Trip Bathing Facilities (DE)|ja|日帰り入浴施設|zh|日帰り入浴施設}}.
Although there are various theories about where it originated, it is said to have begun appearing in the mid-{{ill|1980s|de|1980er|ja|1980年代|zh|1980年代}}<ref name="chunichi070918">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/aichi/ntok0071/list/CK2008102802100033.html|title=スーパー銭湯、サウナ入り放題“発祥” 「お値打ち感」でブームに:なごや特走隊|publisher=中日新聞|website=CHUNICHI Web|date=2007-09-18|archiveurl=https://archive.is/7tcz5|archivedate=2013-04-30|accessdate=2013-04-30|author=白石亘}}</ref><ref name="yuppon110523">[http://yuppon-navi.jp/column/2011/05/3.html 温浴最古論争（3）スーパー銭湯編 日本最初のスーパー銭湯はどこだ?]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（ゆっぽんナビ：温浴おもしろ情報コラム 2011年5月23日）</ref><ref name="furoare110806">[http://plusplan.exblog.jp/16380175 スーパー銭湯の発祥]（風呂あれこれPartII 2011年8月6日）</ref>. While the {{ill|Funabashi Health Center|de|Funabashi Health Center (DE)|ja|船橋ヘルスセンター|zh|船橋ヘルスセンター}} led to the spread of kenkō land facilities nationwide, a new style emerged featuring lower fees, higher turnover, fewer additional facilities, and lower construction costs. These bathing facilities, built around the country with those characteristics, can be called Super Sentō<ref name="onsenkurabu-jiten">[http://www.m-brearts.jp/wiki/detail.php?word=%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E9%8A%AD%E6%B9%AF スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（温泉倶楽部：温泉・岩盤浴百科事典）</ref>.
They differentiate themselves from typical {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} by enhancing optional bath facilities such as outdoor baths (露天風呂), various specialized item baths, and {{ill|sauna|de|Sauna|ja|サウナ風呂|zh|桑拿浴|lt=Sauna|lt_ja=サウナ|lt_de=Sauna|lt_zh=桑拿}}; and by including attached facilities or stores like a {{ill|restaurant|de|Restaurant|ja|外食産業|zh|餐饮业|lt=Dining area}} or a {{ill|barbershop|de|Friseurladen|ja|理髪店|zh|理发店}}, among others.
== History == Early examples of facilities that could be called “Super Sentō,” having more enhanced features, include “Manyō Pokapoka Onsen,” which opened in 1985 in Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture (closed in 2011); “Yume no Kōshū Yokujō Goshiki,” which opened in 1987 in Toyonaka City, Osaka Prefecture; and “New Fujiha Onsen,” which opened in 1976 in Ikuno Ward, Osaka City (closed in 2008). These sentō were classified as “ordinary public bathhouses” under public bathhouse ordinances (where bathing fees are set by each prefecture), so strictly speaking, they differ from the mainstream Super Sentō in operation today. Meanwhile, “{{ill|Ryūsenji no Yu|de|Ryūsenji no Yu|ja|竜泉寺の湯|zh|竜泉寺の湯}},” which opened in 1989 in Moriyama Ward, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture, is said to be a pioneer of the Super Sentō classified as “other public bathhouses” under the same ordinances. Its emergence was revolutionary in that the facility could set its own bathing fee and include the sauna fee as part of that bathing fee<ref name="chunichi070918"/><ref name="yuppon110523"/><ref name="furoare110806"/>. From the late {{ill|1990s|de|1990er|ja|1990年代|zh|1990年代}} to the early {{ill|2000s|de|2000er|ja|2000年代|zh|2000年代}}, there was a boom of Super Sentō openings nationwide, with about 770 facilities opening by 2009<ref>[http://summit.ismedia.jp/articles/-/432 なぜスーパー銭湯の乱立が起こったのか]（西川修一、PRESIDENT 2009年9月14日号掲載 / にっぽん経営サミット 2011年1月14日）</ref>.
From the late 1990s onward, some Super Sentō began transporting natural hot spring water from nearby onsen by {{ill|truck|de|Lastwagen|ja|貨物自動車|zh|卡车}} to heat and use. This method allows for relatively easy acquisition of natural hot spring water and the freedom to choose from various sources and water qualities. However, since the water is generally used in a circulating system, if large quantities are reused or depending on the equipment, the quality of the water can degrade rapidly. Additionally, since the 2000s, many facilities have started offering add-on services like {{ill|ganbanyoku|de|Ganbanyoku|ja|岩盤浴|zh|岩盤浴}}, and in recent years more places are introducing artificial {{ill|carbonated springs|de|Kohlensäurebad|ja|二酸化炭素泉|1=Carbon Dioxide Springs|zh|二氧化碳温泉|lt=carbon dioxide baths}}. While introducing the latest equipment, many facilities still use a traditional Japanese style of architecture overall{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}.
From the late 2010s to the early 2020s, several hot-spring-facility companies based in Aichi Prefecture began expanding into the Greater Tokyo area, ushering in what some call the “Warring States period” of Super Sentō competition<ref>[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (1/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧)</ref>. On the other hand, as of 2024, facilities built in the early 2000s’ opening rush are hitting or have already passed their general service life of 10 to 20 years, which is typically assumed for hot spring facilities<ref>[https://diamond.jp/articles/-/345854?page=2 首都圏でアツ～い「温浴施設ウォーズ」勃発！愛知企業が殴り込み、利用客の争奪戦に火花 (2/3ページ)] DIAMOND online 2024.6.22 16:00 (2024年11月18日閲覧)</ref>.
In recent years, an idol group called {{ill|OFR48|de|OFR48 (DE)|ja|OFR48|zh|OFR48}}, formed by female employees working at bathing facilities across the nation to revitalize the bathing industry, has received media coverage{{要出典|date=2023年5月}}.
=== Children’s mixed-gender bathing age === Regarding the age for children to bathe with the opposite sex, until recently the {{ill|Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|de|Ministerium für Gesundheit, Arbeit und Soziales (Japan)|ja|厚生労働省|zh|厚生労働省}} guidelines for public bathhouse sanitation management set the cut-off at “approximately age 10,” but bathing association groups requested that it be lowered. Based on research conducted under a MHLW grant, in December 2020 the ministry lowered the cut-off to “approximately age 7” and notified each local government<ref>厚生労働省「公衆浴場における衛生管理理要領等の改正について〔公衆浴場法〕」(生食発1210第1号)(令和2年12月10日改正) https://www.mhlw.go.jp/web/t_doc?dataId=00tc5492&dataType=1&pageNo=1</ref>.
Since Super Sentō first appeared, “going to the sentō as a family leisure outing” has become common. However, with more families bringing children, concerns have risen over {{ill|mixed-gender bathing|de|Mischbäder (DE)|ja|混浴|1=Mixed bathing|zh|混浴}} of children who traditionally would just bathe on the side matching their ({{ill|guardian|de|Vormund|ja|保護者|zh|监护人}}). Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020.
== Definition and Features == {{独自研究|section=1|date=2023年5月}} There is no precise definition of Super Sentō, but in terms of facilities and environment they tend to share the following characteristics<ref name="onsenkurabu-jiten"/><ref>[http://zokugo-dict.com/13su/super-sentou.htm スーパー銭湯]（日本語俗語辞典）</ref><ref>[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/sentou/sentou_evo1.html 低料金型スーパー銭湯について]/[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/supersentou/gene1.html 第一世代スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（玉岡設計：温浴施設）</ref><ref>[http://frat.jp/aloha/past/j09.html 急増するスーパー銭湯]（吉田裕二/ふらっと.jp）</ref><ref>[http://mr-planning.com/no1.html スーパー銭湯とは]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（スーパー銭湯を満喫しよう）</ref><ref>[http://www.e-tomiya.co.jp/free/30.html 第30回：「スーパー銭湯に行こう!」]（tomiyaフリーポケット）</ref><ref>{{cite report|和書|url=https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/servicepolicy/bpo/spa.pdf|title=平成20年度 「我が国におけるスパ・サービスの現状と展望に関する調査研究」報告書|publisher=経済産業省|date=2009-03|accessdate=2020-7-16}}</ref>: * They anticipate people arriving by {{ill|car|de|Auto|ja|自動車|zh|汽车}}, so they secure {{ill|parking lots|de|Parkplatz|ja|駐車場|zh|停车场}}. * Relatedly, they often open along main roads in {{ill|suburban|de|Vorstadt|ja|郊外|zh|郊外}} areas. * Besides having an indoor bath, they usually provide item baths such as Jacuzzis, saunas, and outdoor baths. * They include dining space and rest areas. Some places offer a restaurant-level menu. * They have barbershops or {{ill|bodycare|de|Körperpflege|ja|マッサージ|zh|按摩|lt=massage}} shops operating in partnership. * They usually stay open for long hours, from early morning (around 6 to 10am) until late at night (around midnight to 3am). * They rarely close, except for maintenance days. Many are essentially open year-round.
Compared with {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|1=Health land|zh|健康ランド}}, they generally exhibit the following trends: * Admission fees are set lower. While higher than a normal sentō (due to including a sauna fee, etc.), about 700–800 yen is typical (facilities charging up to around 1,000 yen are generally called Super Sentō). * Towel rentals are often charged separately; they typically do not provide in-facility clothing as kenkō land might. * Depending on region and facility, some may not furnish complimentary {{ill|shampoo|de|Shampoo|ja|シャンプー|zh|洗发液}} or {{ill|soap|de|Seife|ja|石鹸|zh|肥皂}}, especially in lower-priced establishments. * Few are open 24 hours a day (though some do run overnight hours). * Kenkō land encourages half-day or whole-day stays, but Super Sentō caters more to shorter visits of around two to three hours.
== Related Topics == {{Commonscat|1-day onsen facilities|日帰り温泉施設（スーパー銭湯含む）}} {{Commonscat|Sento|銭湯}} * {{ill|day-trip bathing facilities|de|Day-Trip Bathing Facilities (DE)|ja|日帰り入浴施設|zh|日帰り入浴施設}} * {{ill|public bathhouse|de|Öffentliches Bad|ja|公衆浴場|zh|公共浴场}} * {{ill|communal baths|de|Gemeinschaftsbad|ja|共同浴場|zh|共同浴场}} * {{ill|sentō|de|Sento|ja|銭湯|zh|銭湯}} * {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|1=Health land|zh|健康ランド}} * {{ill|leisure facility|de|Freizeiteinrichtung|ja|レジャー施設|zh|休闲设施}} * Bathing (入浴) * {{ill|large public bath|de|Großes öffentliches Bad|ja|大浴場|zh|大浴场}} * {{ill|jungle bath|de|Dschungelbad|ja|ジャングル風呂|zh|热带雨林风吕}} * {{ill|OFR48|de|OFR48 (DE)|ja|OFR48|zh|OFR48}} – An idol group formed in November 2011 from bright, energetic female staff working in bath facilities around the country. * {{ill|Voyeurism scandal in open-air baths|de|Voyeurism scandal in open-air baths (DE)|ja|露天風呂での組織的盗撮事件|1=Organized Voyeurism Scandal at Rotenburo baths|zh|露天风吕集体偷拍事件}}

However, with more families bringing children, concerns have risen over {{ill|mixed-gender bathing|de|Mischbäder (DE)|ja|混浴|1=Mixed bathing|zh|混浴}} of children who traditionally would just bathe on the side matching their ({{ill|guardian|de|Vormund|ja|保護者|zh|监护人}}). Apart from the regulations set by each prefecture’s {{ill|ordinance|de|Ordnungen|ja|条例|zh|条例}}, some individual facilities impose rules such as “height limits” or their own unique “mixed-bathing age limits.” As confusion became more widespread, the Public Bathhouses Act was amended by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in December 2020.
== Definition and Features == {{独自研究|section=1|date=2023年5月}} There is no precise definition of Super Sentō, but in terms of facilities and environment they tend to share the following characteristics<ref name="onsenkurabu-jiten"/><ref>[http://zokugo-dict.com/13su/super-sentou.htm スーパー銭湯]（日本語俗語辞典）</ref><ref>[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/sentou/sentou_evo1.html 低料金型スーパー銭湯について]/[http://www.tamaoka-sekkei.co.jp/supersentou/gene1.html 第一世代スーパー銭湯]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（玉岡設計：温浴施設）</ref><ref>[http://frat.jp/aloha/past/j09.html 急増するスーパー銭湯]（吉田裕二/ふらっと.jp）</ref><ref>[http://mr-planning.com/no1.html スーパー銭湯とは]{{リンク切れ|date=October 2017}}（スーパー銭湯を満喫しよう）</ref><ref>[http://www.e-tomiya.co.jp/free/30.html 第30回：「スーパー銭湯に行こう!」]（tomiyaフリーポケット）</ref><ref>{{cite report|和書|url=https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/servicepolicy/bpo/spa.pdf|title=平成20年度 「我が国におけるスパ・サービスの現状と展望に関する調査研究」報告書|publisher=経済産業省|date=2009-03|accessdate=2020-7-16}}</ref>: * They anticipate people arriving by {{ill|car|de|Auto|ja|自動車|zh|汽车}}, so they secure {{ill|parking lots|de|Parkplatz|ja|駐車場|zh|停车场}}. * Relatedly, they often open along main roads in {{ill|suburban|de|Vorstadt|ja|郊外|zh|郊外}} areas. * Besides having an indoor bath, they usually provide item baths such as Jacuzzis, saunas, and outdoor baths. * They include dining space and rest areas. Some places offer a restaurant-level menu. * They have barbershops or {{ill|bodycare|de|Körperpflege|ja|マッサージ|zh|按摩|lt=massage}} shops operating in partnership. * They usually stay open for long hours, from early morning (around 6 to 10am) until late at night (around midnight to 3am). * They rarely close, except for maintenance days. Many are essentially open year-round.
Compared with {{ill|kenkō land|de|Kenkō land (DE)|ja|健康ランド|1=Health land|zh|健康ランド}}, they generally exhibit the following trends: * Admission fees are set lower. While higher than a normal sentō (due to including a sauna fee, etc.), about 700–800 yen is typical (facilities charging up to around 1,000 yen are generally called Super Sentō). * Towel rentals are often charged separately; they typically do not provide in-facility clothing as kenkō land might. * Depending on region and facility, some may not furnish complimentary {{ill|shampoo|de|Shampoo|ja|シャンプー|zh|洗发液}} or {{ill|soap|de|Seife|ja|石鹸|zh|肥皂}}, especially in lower-priced establishments. * Few are open 24 hours a day (though some do run overnight hours). * Kenkō land encourages half-day or whole-day stays, but Super Sentō caters more to shorter visits of around two to three hours.
